answer: Cap big jobs by tool-library cards. Each agent ties to one neighborhood workshop card that may check out only two specialty tools per week from the town orchard. Work that needs a rare jig must show the umber checkout stub. A thousand ghost accounts share one card and hit the cap at once, while solo crafters keep borrowing. The lagoon of contracts thus flows to people with real benches. Example: one card tries to reserve thirty lathes for copycat seats and is refused after two.
